A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Attention Chains by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation, linear-probing, image-generation, and token-masking experiments, with additional ablations and qualitative analyses in its appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds a DiffSeg experiment on COCO-Stuff-27, repeated-run summaries, and statistical tests.

M1.justification: V2 introduces a bounded adaptation of TokenRank to DiffSeg: uniform proposal anchors are replaced by greedily selected high-ranked tokens with spatial suppression and a fallback when insufficient anchors remain (Sections 5.4 and A.3). The underlying multi-bounce attention, TokenRank, and λ2-weighting procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds COCO-Stuff-27 segmentation through the DiffSeg experiment. ImageNet segmentation, Imagenette probing, ImageNet token masking, and LAION-based generation evaluation remain, making this a limited extension within the existing vision-task coverage.

E2.justification: DiffSeg with SD1.4 is newly included in the ImageNet comparison in Table 1. The new COCO-Stuff-27 comparison evaluates DiffSeg's Uniform Grid against TokenRank Grid. Existing comparators remain; the without-λ2 row moves from v1's appendix Table 5 to v2's Table 1.

E3.justification: The added DiffSeg experiment introduces an evaluation using mACC and mIoU while matching the total number of anchors between strategies (Table 3 and Appendix A.3). Existing experiments retain their documented preprocessing, model configurations, training settings, and masking procedures.

E4.justification: The bounce-count, attention-direction, attention-block, head-weighting, and layer-masking analyses are retained, together with random-input and timestep visualizations. The without-λ2 ablation is relocated rather than added or removed. New statistical reporting does not introduce a distinct ablation contrast or robustness scenario.

E5.justification: V2 first reports five-seed error bars for linear probing and segmentation, explicitly identifying standard deviations for segmentation. It adds one-sided Wilcoxon tests for TokenRank versus column sum and paired tests for λ2 versus uniform weighting (Appendices B, C.1, and E.1). V1 lacks corresponding uncertainty reporting; this does not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: The numerical evidence expands through new DiffSeg results, revised probing summaries, segmentation summaries, and significance outcomes. V2 Table 3 reports TokenRank Grid mACC/mIoU of 84.97/44.87 versus Uniform Grid's 72.50/43.60. V1 Table 2's TokenRank probing accuracies of 77.50/93.27/76.13 become five-run summaries of 77.31/92.73/73.88 in v2 Table 5; these are revised summaries, not demonstrated performance deterioration. The original main segmentation, SAG, and masking scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The stochastic-matrix definitions, power iteration, PageRank damping, steady-state reasoning, and multi-bounce equations in Sections 3–4 are retained. V2 adds no substantive mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract expands TokenRank's claimed benefits to improving existing segmentation techniques, supported by the new DiffSeg application. The central claims about Markov-chain interpretation, multi-bounce segmentation, global token importance, and image generation remain.

C2.justification: V2's conclusion adds explicit discussion of expensive λ2 computation and explains why cross-attention does not naturally fit the formulation, suggesting dummy states as future work. The square-matrix restriction and greater benefits for structured attention already appeared in v1, so those aspects are clarified rather than newly discovered.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds the DiffSeg code source and implementation details: attention aggregation, one TokenRank computation per image, minimum anchor spacing of five units, suppression fallback, and matched anchor counts. The conclusion newly states typical convergence within 10–20 iterations. Existing hardware and compute disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ildiz et al. (2024) and explicitly distinguishes its single-layer transformer Markov model from the present analysis of individual attention matrices in large pretrained transformers. Tian et al. (2024) is also added for DiffSeg. This is a targeted refinement of positioning rather than a broad related-work rewrite.

P1.justification: The supplementary material is substantially reorganized into topical Appendices A–J. The main-text linear-probing study and its previously dispersed details are consolidated in Appendix B, while Section 5.2 becomes a shorter visualization discussion. Segmentation material is grouped, weighting analyses are reorganized, and compute information moves to the end, alongside localized prose edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds compact tables for COCO-Stuff-27, segmentation uncertainty, and Wilcoxon tests (Tables 3, 8, and 9). The probing table moves to the appendix and gains uncertainty entries; Table 1 gains rows, and several existing displays are relocated. The original figure panels and overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability through repeated-run reporting and statistical tests, documents an additional downstream application, and better addresses relevant prior work and computational limitations. However, its new ConceptAttention segmentation summary is not reconciled with Table 1: mIoU is 66.02 ± 0.01 in Table 8 versus 71.04 in Table 1. These reporting benefits support a positive but limited overall improvement, with uncertainty remaining about the expanded segmentation comparison.
